chief_complaint: clean cut on index finger palmar aspect from knife
hpi_details: A 32-year-old female presents to the clinic with clean cut on index finger palmar aspect from knife. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks the sharp kitchen knife slipped while slicing carrots and cut straight through the skin into the flesh of her finger.
concerns: She is worried that she severed a tendon or nerve in her finger that might permanently prevent her from typing at her office desk.
expectations: She hopes to have the wound cleaned, numbed, and neatly stitched or glued together, along with an updated tetanus booster.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Finger Laceration is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Finger Laceration: Check two-point sensation, FDS/FDP function, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

history.answer: I accidentally cut the palm side of my right index finger with a kitchen knife about an hour ago, and I came in to have it checked.
I was slicing vegetables for dinner when the knife slipped and sliced into my finger.
It happened about an hour ago, around six in the evening.
It is on the palm side of my right index finger, and it looks to be about an inch long.
The knife was clean stainless steel, and no piece of the blade broke off or stayed in the cut.
It was bleeding steadily at first, but after I pressed a clean towel on it for ten minutes, the bleeding slowed down to a trickle.
The tip of my finger does not feel numb or tingly at all. Sensation feels completely normal.
I can still bend and straighten the tip and middle joint of my finger, though bending it pulls on the cut and stings.
The cut has a sharp stinging pain that throbs a bit, around a 4 out of 10 in severity.
I rinsed it briefly under cool tap water, applied direct pressure with a clean cloth, and kept my hand elevated.
No, there is no redness spreading up my finger, no pus, and I have not had any chills or fever.
I received a tetanus shot about five years ago after scraping my knee.
I am right-handed, so this happened to my dominant hand.
No, nothing like that. It was entirely an accident while preparing dinner.
I have been feeling a bit run down from work lately, but I did not get dizzy, lightheaded, or faint.
I think the kitchen knife just slipped while I was cutting up carrots and sliced straight through the skin into the flesh.
I'm worried that I might have cut a tendon or nerve and won't be able to bend my finger properly to type for work.
I was hoping you could numb and stitch or glue the cut closed so it heals cleanly, and give me a tetanus shot if I need one.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions, no diabetes, and no bleeding problems.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I am not taking any prescription medicines, blood thinners, or over-the-counter drugs.
I have no known allergies to medications, latex, or antiseptics.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only have a glass of wine socially once or twice a month.
I work as an office accountant and live in an apartment with my husband.
My parents and siblings are all healthy, with no history of bleeding disorders or poor healing.
My last period started about two weeks ago, and my cycles are always regular.
We use condoms consistently, and there is no chance that I could be pregnant.

exam.finding: Well-appearing woman in no acute distress, holding a clean dry dressing over her right hand with no active bleeding.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.7 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are anicteric.
Clean linear 2 cm laceration on the volar aspect of the right index finger over the middle phalanx, with no foreign body, tissue loss, or surrounding erythema.
Full active flexion against resistance at both the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints, confirming intact flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus function.
Static two-point discrimination is intact at 4 mm along both radial and ulnar digital nerve distributions distal to the wound.
Radial and ulnar pulses are 2+ bilaterally, and capillary refill is under 2 seconds at the right index fingertip.
Full active and passive range of motion of all right index finger joints with no collateral ligament laxity.
